name: zero-gale-column-delete-reinsert
statement: If a Gale column vanishes (say c1 = 0) the corresponding sign is free: St = {±1} x S't and |St|/2^m = |S't|/2^(m-1); linearly W = R*e1 (+) W'. A residual certificate for the reduced coordinate family lifts with the same dimension; the free coordinate contributes at most one new quotient class, exactly matching the increase in ambient rank, so dgeo(F') ≤ 2 implies dgeo(F) ≤ 2. By induction, arbitrarily many zero columns may be deleted and reinserted without changing density or invalidating a low-dimensional certificate; a hypothetical distance-three counterexample remains a counterexample after deletion.
dependencies: Gale fibre setup St = {x ∈ {±1}^m : Cx = t} (p.18)
notes: Repairs an implicit step in the earlier project tree; justifies reducing to nonzero Gale columns before the finite normal-form analysis.

name: intrinsic-cube-model
statement: Assume the affine fibre spans its expected affine flat and the homogenized displayed coordinates are projectively simple and coordinate-full. Choose a basis g1,...,gR of the full dual of the homogenized antipodal fibre A_hat_t (R = m-2) and define Phi: W_hat -> R^R by Phi(w) = (g1(w),...,gR(w)). Spanning makes Phi an isomorphism; each gi is sign-valued on the fibre, so Phi(A_hat_t) lies in the intrinsic cube {±1}^R and is antipodal. Coordinate-fullness gives closure: any cube point satisfying every intrinsic full-dual equation pulls back into W_hat ∩ {±1}^(m+1) = A_hat_t. The intrinsic image is full closed with exactly R+3 projective full-dual forms (the m+1 = R+3 displayed coordinates).
dependencies: affine homogenization setup C_hat = [C | -t], h = homogenizer (p.18)
notes: Connects the affine problem to finite enumeration of full-closed antipodal cube subsets with no unproved closure hypothesis. Hats flattened by extraction ('b At', 'c W') and reconstructed as A_hat_t, W_hat.

name: saturated-shared-h-plane
statement: In the shared-h setting an optimal homogenized residual plane R_hat is SATURATED when all of: k_{F_hat}(R_hat) = r+1 (signed projective class count one above the old ambient budget r); h ∉ R_hat; the quotient class [h]_{R_hat} contains an old form; dim S = 2, where S is the span of the old signed differences that survive from R_hat; and restriction to ker h creates no additional merger. Here h is the homogenizer coordinate form.
notes: [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN] 'kb F ( bR) = r + 1' read as k_{F_hat}(R_hat) = r+1; r is the old class budget (r = m-3 in the m=8 pages).

name: forced-exceptional-plane-proposition
statement: Assume the old affine family has dgeo(F) = 3 while the completed homogeneous corank-three theorem yields dgeo(F_hat) ≤ 2. Then dgeo(F_hat) = 2 exactly and EVERY optimal homogenized residual plane R_hat is saturated, with no additional merger after restriction to ker h. Each failure of saturation would already descend to an old residual of dimension ≤ 2, contradicting dgeo(F) = 3: if the h-class contained no old form, deleting h would remove a quotient class; if h ∈ R_hat, restriction would lose a residual dimension; if restriction created another merger, the old class count would fall below the threshold. Thus a single shared-h geometry is isolated for the finite argument to exclude.
notes: Stated as AUDITED PROPOSITION.

name: collision-forest-classification
statement: Three collision edges in the saturated residual plane have exactly four unsigned forest shapes: 3K2, P3+K2, P4, K1,3. Exact rational reconstruction enumerates 16 primitive dependence triples per shape, then filters by projective simplicity and the global two-extra-form budget. Survivor counts (primitive/simple/budget/balanced): 3K2: 16/16/4/4; P3+K2: 16/8/2/2; P4: 16/1/1/1; K1,3: 16/3/3/3. Every survivor is balanced on support four or six and contains the homogenizer; setting h = 1 leaves an old support of size three or five with a highly constrained conditional state set.
notes: Canonical verifier uses integer arithmetic and Python fractions.Fraction; no floating tolerance enters the table.

name: m8-support3-and-distinct5-normal-forms
statement: m = 8 is the finite endpoint (target-uniform flag bounds close effective sizes m = 9, 10, 11). Old support size three: planar spectrum type (1,2,2); the exact checker enumerates all eight target multisets, reconstructs integer primal coordinate forms on ker C, and finds a residual certificate of rank ≤ 2 in all eight cases. Old support size five with three distinct planar directions A, B, A+B: admissible root configurations reduce to twelve; every one is projectively simple and has an exact rank-two residual certificate leaving at most r = 8-3 = 5 signed projective quotient classes. These are exhaustive normal forms, not random samples.
dependencies: target-uniform flag bounds / repaired 12+3 coupling (external, pp.15-17)
notes: Audit explains why the balanced local relation forces exactly these planar multiplicity patterns and why coordinate reorientations omit no affine target type. Matches packet verifier output: q3 normalforms=8 simple=8 dgeo<=2=8; q5 distinct normalforms=12 simple=12 dgeo<=2=12.

name: m8-repeated-AAB-family
statement: The repeated-direction (A,A,B) family at m = 8, the largest finite search, reduces through the exact chain 93312 -> 2934 -> 76 -> 20 -> 12: derived connected-graph constructions -> canonically sorted distinct target multisets -> high conditional-count threshold -> direction condition -> projective simplicity. For each of the twelve survivors the verifier constructs exact integer primal coordinate forms, enumerates signed-difference residual lines and planes, and asserts a rank-at-most-two certificate with at most five quotient classes. Eight cases have conditional total 14 and four have total 15.
notes: Positive certificates checked by exact rational rank and class-count operations; every final survivor tested directly. Matches packet output: direction-ok=20 simple=12 dgeo<=2=12.

name: cpp-float-key-plane-dedup
statement: The earlier C++ shared-h project deduplicated candidate residual planes with a floating-point key and skipped purported duplicates. As exact evidence this route fails: a float key can conflate distinct planes, so completeness of the surviving classification is uncertifiable. Condition of failure: whenever the classification is cited as exact or exhaustive. The canonical Python verifier removes the vulnerability via exact rational rank and class-count operations and by testing every final survivor directly.
source: dossier p.24, p.27 (packet S1, S3, S4)
notes: Old floating-point routines are retained as evidence only and must not be called exact (p.27).

name: m-le-7-intrinsic-enumeration
statement: For m ≤ 7 the intrinsic rank is R = m-2 ≤ 5. The exact checker enumerates every nonempty antipodal subset of {±1}^R, retains spanning full-closed fibres with exactly R+3 projective full-dual forms, and searches for a residual line. Counts (subsets/spanning/closed/|D|=R+3/dgeo=1): R=2: 3/1/1/0/0; R=3: 15/5/5/0/0; R=4: 255/151/123/0/0; R=5: 65535/60879/16907/2320/2320. Every rank-five corank-three fibre in the class has a one-dimensional intrinsic residual certificate; the restriction inequality dgeo(F) ≤ dgeo(F_hat)+1 then gives dgeo(F) ≤ 2. No old distance-three shared-h obstruction exists at m ≤ 7.
notes: Subset counts equal 2^(2^(R-1))-1 antipodal subsets - consistent. Reproduced verbatim in the packet verifier output: FULL r=5: subsets=65535 spanning=60879 closed=16907 corank3=2320 dgeo1=2320. Per p.27 the rank-five run is certified by archived output + checksum; local and m=8 modes were rerun fresh.

name: restriction-inequality-affine-descent
statement: dgeo(F) ≤ dgeo(F_hat) + 1: descending from the homogenized family F_hat (ambient dimension one larger, dim W_hat = m-2 vs dim W = m-3) to the old affine family F costs at most one geometric residual dimension.
notes: Stated and applied on p.25; its proof belongs to the shared-h analysis outside pp.19-36 (S5). Recorded here as used.

name: integrated-affine-rank-three-density-theorem
statement: Under affine spanning, projective simplicity, and coordinate-full homogenization, an affine fibre of density greater than 27/512 cannot have old geometric distance three. Structure: homogeneous compression yields an optimal residual plane; if it descends with any slack the old distance is ≤ 2; otherwise it has the saturated shared-h pattern, the balanced local relation reduces the old support to three or five coordinates, and long directions, flag estimates, planar spectra, the m = 8 exact normal forms, and the m ≤ 7 intrinsic enumeration cover every possible effective size. In each case either the density is ≤ 27/512 or an old rank-two residual certificate contradicts distance three.
notes: Quantifier: under the distance-three hypothesis EVERY optimal homogenized plane must be exceptional, so excluding any selected one suffices. Density threshold 27/512 ~ 0.0527. Finite components certified per p.27; this is a deterministic local theorem, not the determinant conjecture.

name: shared-h-verifier-provenance
statement: The canonical shared-h verifier certifies three finite claims over Q: (1) the complete local three-edge relation table; (2) all m = 8 normal forms including the repeated-direction chain; (3) every intrinsic full-closed antipodal fibre through rank five. The archived complete run ends 'PASS mode=all: all asserted identities and certificates verified over Q' and its SHA-256 is recorded in the source packet. For this dossier the local and m = 8 modes were rerun successfully; the full rank-five enumeration is preserved as archived output with matching checker checksum rather than silently represented as a fresh full run.
notes: Separates exact finite arithmetic from analytic completeness: the checker validates finite tables and certificates, while the reduction and descent arguments are analytic proofs (cf. p.17).

name: random-slice-experiments-evidence-only
statement: Random rank-six and rank-eight slice experiments from the earlier project are numerical evidence only about higher-rank shared-h behavior. They carry no exactness claim and must not be cited as certificates; the canonical rational checker and the analytic bridge lemmas are the proof-relevant objects.
notes: Recorded to prevent status inflation of floating-point or sampled computations.

name: linear-entropy-rigidity-theorem-needed
statement: STILL NEEDED: dcb(A) ≤ C*ell(A) for every spanning, full-closed, antipodal sign fibre A ⊆ {±1}^r, uniformly over the real/no-wrap setting and the odd finite fields used by the moment argument. The recursion needs the stronger rooted form dim((R+R_<)/R_<) ≤ C*L(Q|W) together with connector absorption R ∩ span(W) ⊆ R_<. An intrinsic sufficient formulation is the evaluation-Rado lower bound qev(A) ≥ r - C*ell(A). Proven substitutes are NOT this theorem: the unconditional bound is exponential in ell; bounded congestion gives linear quotient rank without automatic absorption; exact cycle certificates cover a structured class. Remaining block: the dense, connector-incoherent complement.
notes: Extraction-flattened 'dim R + R< / R<' read as dim((R+R_<)/R_<). Any universal constant must satisfy C ≥ 1/log2(4/3) = 2.40942... (see nae-three-circuit-constant-lower-bound).

name: nae-three-circuit-constant-lower-bound
statement: The product of NAE three-circuits shows that any universal constant C in a linear entropy-rigidity theorem dcb(A) ≤ C*ell(A) must satisfy C ≥ 1/log2(4/3) = 2.40942...; in particular no constant-one version of the theorem can hold.
notes: Cited on p.28 as calibration of the open target; the underlying rooted-NAE construction is detailed outside pp.19-36. Numeric check: log2(4/3) = 0.41504, reciprocal 2.4094 - matches.

name: two-shadow-graph-and-weighted-batching
statement: For sign-valued rows ha on S = {x ∈ {±1}^r : ha.x ∈ {±1} for every a} (signed-coordinate rows discarded), let Ea = supp(ha). The two-shadow graph Gamma on [r] has an edge ij whenever some Ea contains both i and j. Batching data: fix a maximum matching P1,...,PN of Gamma; greedily choose a remaining pair, select a witness support Es containing it, and remove the batch Bs of all remaining matching pairs meeting Es; set as = |Bs|, Vs = union of the pairs in Bs, Us = Es ∩ Vs.
dependencies: sign fibre and entropy defect ell (p.5)

name: weighted-batching-lemma
statement: In the greedy weighted batching: |Us| ≥ as + 1 for every batch, the sets Us are pairwise disjoint, and an earlier witness support is disjoint from every later Ut. The batching is weighted: a witness meeting many disjoint matching pairs is charged by its full Littlewood-Offord atom loss rather than by a single 3/4 factor multiplied by its support size. This is the step that improves the old common-core size O((1+ell)*4^ell) to O(4^ell).
notes: Extraction 'O((1 + ℓ)4ℓ)' and 'O(4ℓ)' reconstructed as O((1+ell)*4^ell) and O(4^ell) (superscripts flattened).

name: reverse-triangular-exposure
statement: Condition on all signs outside the union of the Us and expose the disjoint blocks in reverse order Uk, Uk-1, ..., U1. When Us is peeled, every earlier selected-row indicator is independent of the variables being exposed (earlier witness supports avoid later U-sets), and variables in earlier Ut remain arbitrary parameters in the target. This yields Pr(hs.X ∈ {±1} | previous exposure) ≤ psi(as+1), and multiplying in reverse order gives 2^(-ell) ≤ prod_s psi(as+1). Audit repair: one must use Us, not all of Es; if |Us| > as+1, first condition on the extra active coordinates, then apply the (as+1)-term atom bound. With that repair the argument is rigorous over R and the specified finite fields.
notes: The quantifier repair is one of the six audit repairs recorded on p.37.

name: two-point-atom-bound
statement: Target-uniform two-point atom bound: with u active variables (all coefficients nonzero), the probability of hitting either of two prescribed targets is at most psi(u) = min(3/4, 2^(1-u)*binom(u, floor(u/2))) ≤ min(3/4, 2/sqrt(u)). For u = 2 the 3/4 estimate is the nondegenerate parallelogram bound; for u ≥ 3 it is twice the central-binomial one-point mass. Over Fp the correct statement is NOT merely 'no wrap': invoke the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem when u < p and all active coefficients are nonzero, then take a union bound over the two targets.
notes: Extraction '21-u (u over floor u/2)' reconstructed as 2^(1-u)*binom(u,floor(u/2)); '2 sqrt-u' as 2/sqrt(u). Independent audit harness exhaustively checked coefficient multisets u = 2..8, primes ≤ 13 with p > u (p.37: FINITE_FIELD_LO PASS coefficient_multisets=4370).

name: atom-charges-cs-beta
statement: Charges: cs = -log2 psi(as+1) and beta = log2(4/3). Then cs ≥ beta for every batch (psi ≤ 3/4), and sum_s cs ≤ ell (from 2^(-ell) ≤ prod_s psi(as+1)). These charges are the bridge from conditional atom losses to a graph-theoretic core size.

name: weighted-compression-arithmetic
statement: From the atom bound, as + 1 ≤ 4*4^(cs). With C* = sum_s cs and 4^beta = 16/9, a convexity calculation gives (sum_s 4^(cs))/4^(C*) ≤ m*(16/9)^(-(m-1)) ≤ 9/8, where m is the number of nonempty batches (the trivial N = 0 case is separated first). Therefore N = sum_s as ≤ 4*sum_s 4^(cs) ≤ (9/2)*4^ell. The endpoints of a maximum matching form a vertex cover C of Gamma, so |C| ≤ 2N ≤ 9*4^ell. No two-shadow edge survives outside a vertex cover, hence every row support contains at most one coordinate outside C.
notes: Constant 9 explicitly not claimed sharp; the structural gain is paying dense rows their full atom loss, eliminating the old 1+ell factor. Arithmetic independently re-derived here: max over m ≥ 1 of m*(9/16)^(m-1) is 9/8 at m = 2 - checks. Superscripts flattened in extraction ('9 4ℓ' = 9*4^ell).

name: weighted-two-shadow-compression-theorem
statement: Let K = R, or K = Fp with odd p > r. Suppose S = {x ∈ {±1}^r : ha.x ∈ {±1} for every a} with |S| = 2^(r-ell). After discarding signed-coordinate rows, there is a set C ⊆ [r] with |C| ≤ 9*4^ell such that |supp(ha) setminus C| ≤ 1 for every a: every sign-valued row is a core form plus at most one private coordinate (a star over one common core). This is an unconditional high-corank theorem, applying independently of any low-corank decomposition. Explicit limitation: the core is exponential in ell, so this result alone cannot yield the desired uniform LINEAR entropy-rigidity estimate.
notes: Independent audit passed after six precise repairs (p.37). Creates the star-over-core form needed by the entropy-sharpened residual argument and enlarges the controlled endpoint range.

name: conditionally-free-coordinate-and-N0
statement: Given the common core C, every row can be written ha(x) = qa(xC) + lambda_a*xj with at most one j ∉ C. Coordinate j is CONDITIONALLY FREE if both signs of Xj occur above some realized core value XC = c; evaluating the row at the two points forces qa(c) = 0 and lambda_a = ±1. N0 := the set of outside coordinates that are never conditionally free, i.e. not free above any realized core pattern.

name: entropy-sharpened-residual-rank-theorem
statement: For every realized core pattern the entire vector X_N0 is deterministic, so H(XC, X_N0) = H(XC); entropy then gives |N0| ≤ ell. Selecting the signed coordinate lambda_a*xj for each conditionally free private coordinate leaves all residuals in the coordinate span of C ∪ N0, proving d(H) ≤ 9*4^ell + ell and consequently dcb(A) ≤ 9*4^(ell(A)) + ell(A) for every spanning full-closed antipodal sign fibre (over R and the odd finite fields of the compression theorem). The quantifier 'never free for EVERY realized core pattern' is essential; weaker coordinatewise conditioning would not justify the entropy identity.
notes: The packet's strongest unconditional global estimate (also quoted p.2). Exponential in ell - it is NOT the linear target of the open gap on p.28.

name: conditional-exponential-cyclic-block-theorem
statement: For a rooted block with boundary W, private sign basis Q of size q, and conditional defect L(Q|W) = q - H(Q|W), the target-uniform batching proof can be run conditionally on the boundary. It yields selectors whose new residual rank modulo the boundary obeys dim((R + span W)/span W) ≤ 9*4^(L(Q|W)) + L(Q|W). This is a genuine affine, target-uniform theorem: the selected rows may have boundary-dependent targets, and the Littlewood-Offord bounds are uniform in those targets. It does NOT prove connector absorption: quotient rank is controlled after modding out the whole boundary span, but a residual combination could still produce a new pure boundary direction.
notes: Extraction-flattened 'dim R + span W / span W' read as dim((R+span W)/span W). The packet deliberately keeps quotient compression and absorption as separate assertions.

name: connector-absorption-gap
statement: OPEN: connector absorption for the exponential conditional theorem. The rooted global theorem needs every pure boundary residual created by a child block to lie in the ancestor-paid space R_< (R ∩ span(W) ⊆ R_<); the conditional exponential estimate controls only the quotient rank modulo the whole boundary span. Without absorption the same boundary direction can be charged again at each generation of the recursive block tree, producing a depth loss even when every local quotient bound is linear or exponential.
source: dossier p.35 (context p.8; packet S6, S7)
notes: p.8 (outside this chunk) records an exact kernel criterion for absorption and a full-closed NAE-star counterexample showing bounded support alone does not imply it (S14).

name: endpoint-range-of-exponential-theorem
statement: In the component encoding, sequences with k = O(n/log n) and ell -> infinity are controlled whenever 4^ell = o(ell*log n); the residual error from 9*4^ell + ell is then negligible against the leading saving -(n-r)*ell. Equivalently the uniformly controlled range includes ell ≤ (1/2)*log2 log n + (1/2)*log2 log log n - omega(1). Quantifier (audit-corrected): if a sequence merely fails the little-o condition, the corresponding lower bound on ell is valid only along a subsequence where 4^ell/(ell*log n) stays bounded below - not an every-index conclusion for an oscillating sequence. Fixed-defect cases are handled separately by finite-core enumeration.
notes: 'Controlled' is relative to the moment-argument encoding; this does NOT decide the conjecture, and a substantial regime remains where 4^ell is too large to pay directly. Threshold re-checked: at the stated ell bound, 4^ell = (log n)(log log n)*2^(-omega(1)) = o(ell*log n). Superscripts flattened in extraction.
